chunks: And Abu Ali al-Ash'ari narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi from Ubays ibn Hisham from Thabit from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about al-mula'ana (mutual cursing) when they had performed it and separated, and the husband later said, 'The child is mine,' while disproving himself (by his own statement or evidence). He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the woman, she is not returned to him, but I return the child to him. I do not leave his child (the one from the other woman) as having no inheritance. If his father does not claim him, then his maternal uncles (from the father's side) inherit him, and they do not inherit from him. If anyone claims him, saying, "O son of the fornicator," he is flogged with the fixed punishment.'

key_terms.أَخْوَال: Maternal uncles: Specifically the brothers of the mother, though context here implies paternal uncles inheriting from the child.
key_terms.الْحَدَّ: The fixed punishment: Referring to the specific corporal punishment for fornication or false accusation.
key_terms.الْمُلاَعَنَة: Mula'ana: A ritual of mutual cursing used to resolve disputes over paternity.
key_terms.الْوَلَد: The child: Referring to the offspring whose paternity is in dispute.
key_terms.مِيرَاث: Inheritance: The right to inherit from the deceased.

ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance and paternity rulings after the ritual of Mula'ana in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific inheritance dynamics of a child born from *mula'ana*, establishing that the child is attributed to the father but excluded from his general inheritance if not formally claimed. It further details the collateral inheritance line, noting that the maternal uncles (*akhwal*) inherit the child, a ruling that highlights the distinct Shia jurisprudential approach to paternity disputes compared to other schools. The mention of flogging for false claimants underscores the legal weight of the *kudib* (illegitimate) status in personal status law.
